summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 60 views. The best videos are about robots and sound-triggered gadgets (clap switch, gyro, PIR, line follower) and get the most likes, saves and shares. Everyday-device videos (taps, doors, smoke alarms, touchscreens) and the one English video are weak, and the newest videos have not had time to grow yet.
winningPattern: A hobby-robot or Arduino-module subject (gyro robot, clap switch, PIR, line follower, IR obstacle robot) with a surprising 'it doesn't X, it only Y' or 'without this, it fails' hook. Titles are short Hinglish with one emoji and #shorts, posted mainly for Instagram Reels. Videos from Oct 26 to Nov 5 with this style reached 1,200-1,400 IG views, while question-style 'How does the tap/door/alarm know?' titles stayed under 600.
doMore: Make robot and maker-module videos (gyro, line follower, IR, clap switch, mic), the topics students want to build
Open with a bold twist like 'X nahi karta, sirf Y karta hai' or 'Iske bina robot gir jaata'
Show a quick visible demo of the failure or surprise in the first 2 seconds
End with a save-worthy tip or part name so viewers save it for their project
Make follow-ups to winners such as clap switch, PIR and IR robot, with new angles
Cross-check YouTube separately: test one different title or thumbnail style there, since it lags far behind IG
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise Pata Chalta Hai? 🤔' videos on everyday gadgets like taps, lift doors and street lights
Posting near-duplicate topics (several smoke detector, IR and tap videos) in the same week
Mixing in English narration, since it has no IG reach and little traction
